subject: computer-science

moments.title: Facebook launched at Harvard
moments.body: TheFacebook launches on 4 February 2004 at Harvard. Within a month, half of Harvard undergraduates have profiles. It expands to other Ivy League universities, then all US colleges (2005), then global (2006). News Feed (2006) is initially hated by users; the iPhone (2007) and the mobile app dominate engagement.
moments.takeaway: A college-only social network reached 3 billion monthly active users within 20 years. The transformation of how humans talk to each other happened within a single career.

moments.title: YouTube launches and is acquired
moments.who: Steve Chen, Chad Hurley, Jawed Karim; Google
moments.body: YouTube launches in February 2005 from an apartment in San Mateo. The first video, 'Me at the zoo' (23 April 2005, 19 seconds), is uploaded by Karim. Google acquires YouTube in October 2006 for $1.65 billion in stock. Now over 500 hours of video are uploaded every minute.
moments.takeaway: A site for sharing home videos became the world's largest online video platform within 18 months.

now.title: Social media today
now.body: TikTok (ByteDance, 2016 global) overtook Facebook and YouTube for time-spent among younger users. EU Digital Services Act (2022) and content moderation legal debates shape platform behaviour. The 2024 US TikTok ban legislation and 2025 partial divestment showed how platform geopolitics evolved. Misinformation, polarisation and youth mental-health concerns are ongoing.
now.open_questions: Can platforms be regulated for safety while preserving speech and innovation? Different jurisdictions are settling at very different points.

reflection: Facebook's 'move fast and break things' motto was abandoned in 2014. The things it broke included some elements of democratic discourse. The cost of growth-at-all-costs cultures is now better understood.
